verses.1: At that time, sleep did not come to the best of men, Shatrughna, as he lay thinking about the excellent song of Rama, which had many meanings.
verses.2: Having heard his (Lava's and Kusha's) very sweet singing, accompanied by string instruments and rhythm, the night quickly passed for the great-souled Shatrughna.
verses.3: When that night had dawned, Shatrughna, having performed his morning rituals, spoke words with folded hands to the chief of sages, Valmiki.
verses.4: Shatrughna said, "O venerable one, I wish to see Rama, the delight of the Raghus, and I wish to be permitted by you to go with these ascetics of firm vows."
verses.5: Having embraced Shatrughna, the tormentor of foes, who was speaking thus, Valmiki sent him off to Rama.
verses.6: Having saluted the revered sage Valmiki and mounted his splendid chariot, he swiftly departed for Ayodhya, eager to behold Rama.
verses.7: The glorious and mighty-armed Shatrughna, the delight of the Ikshvakus, entered the beautiful city and proceeded to where the highly effulgent Rama resided.
verses.8: He saw Rama, whose face resembled the full moon, seated amidst his ministers, appearing like the thousand-eyed Indra surrounded by gods.
verses.9: Having saluted the great-souled Rama, who shone as if with his own splendor and possessed true valor, he spoke with folded hands.
verses.10: O great king, I have accomplished all that you commanded: the wicked Lavana has been slain, and his city has been established.
verses.11: O Rama, twelve years have passed without you, and I, separated from you, O King, am no longer able to live here.
verses.12: Therefore, O Rama of immeasurable valor, grant me this favor, for I cannot stay away much longer, just like a motherless calf.
verses.13: Having embraced Shatrughna who was speaking thus, Rama said, "O brave one, do not despair, for this is not the conduct befitting a Kshatriya."
verses.14: O Raghava, kings do not become dejected during separations, for indeed, our subjects must be protected according to the duty of a Kshatriya.
verses.15: O brave one, O best among men, you should come to Ayodhya from time to time to see me, and you will also return to your own city.
verses.16: Rama tells Shatrughna that he is dearer than life itself, but the protection of the kingdom is an essential duty.
verses.17: Therefore, O Kakutstha, stay here for seven nights, and thereafter you shall proceed to Mathura with your servants, army, and vehicles.
verses.18: Having heard these righteous and heartfelt words of Rama, Shatrughna, with a humble voice, simply replied, "Indeed."
verses.19: And the great archer Shatrughna, having stayed there for seven nights as per Rama's command, began preparations for his departure.
verses.20: Having bid farewell to the great-souled Rama of true valor, and also to Bharata and Lakshmana, he then ascended a great chariot.
verses.21: After being accompanied for a long distance by the great-souled Lakshmana and Bharata, Shatrughna then quickly proceeded to the city of Ayodhya. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 72 ।। Thus ends the seventy-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
